lens: Swipe discovery (Tinder/Hinge): swipe through personas and quick drills
name: Swipe-to-Rehearse Coach Studio
one_liner: A dark-first live-call cockpit with real-time coaching and rubric scoring, a filterable persona library with a swipe-deck drill mode, and an AI wizard that drafts personas from any source, built on shadcn/ui and visibly powered by OpenAI models.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the swipe lens for quick drills only: a Tinder/Hinge-style deck where right runs a 90-second objection drill, left skips, and up saves. Changed it for the main library. Mobbin results (Klaviyo content-block library, Recraft style library) show filtered card grids win when someone compares dozens of options, and a swipe-only library hides choice. Swipe is a mode, not the default. Competitors Yoodli and Second Nature both claim practice and live calls are graded against one rubric; this design adopts that as a core principle.

ui_stack.name: shadcn/ui
ui_stack.role: Component system: Button, Card, Tabs, Dialog, Sheet, Command, Chart, Drawer
ui_stack.why: Copy-in source code the repo owns, no runtime lock-in, documented Tailwind v4 and React 19 support, and contributors can read and PR components directly.

ui_stack.name: Tailwind CSS v4
ui_stack.role: Styling with tokens in one CSS theme file replacing tailwind.config
ui_stack.why: CSS-first tokens make light and dark modes a single source of truth and retire the hand-rolled .card/.btn-primary classes gradually.

ui_stack.name: Radix UI primitives (via shadcn)
ui_stack.role: Accessible dialog, tabs, tooltip, popover, and the swipe deck's keyboard fallback
ui_stack.why: Keyboard and screen-reader behavior is correct by default, which matters for an open-source reference app.

ui_stack.name: vaul (shadcn Drawer)
ui_stack.role: Mobile coach bottom sheet with peek, half, and full snap points
ui_stack.why: Native-feeling sheet gestures without custom touch code.

ui_stack.name: cmdk
ui_stack.role: Command palette on every screen: jump to a persona, start a drill, open a debrief
ui_stack.why: Power users and contributors move without the mouse.

ui_stack.name: Recharts via shadcn chart
ui_stack.role: Score trend, distribution, and skill heat map
ui_stack.why: Replaces hand-built bars with real charts and tooltips at low cost.

ui_stack.name: motion (Framer Motion)

ui_stack.why: Spring physics for gestures; motion collapses to fades under reduced-motion settings.

ui_stack.name: Geist Sans and Geist Mono (Google Fonts)
ui_stack.role: UI and headline type; mono for timers, scores, and timestamps
ui_stack.why: Replaces Inter plus Sora with a precise, developer-tool feel that suits an open-source AI product. lucide-react, zod and react-hook-form stay.

palette.use: Page background; the live call is always on the dark canvas.
Cards, sheets, and the coach panel.
Primary buttons and anything AI-written. Reserved so reps always know what the model produced.
Whisper cues and objection alerts only.
Score losses, errors, and the End call control.

design_language.typography: Geist Sans for all UI and headlines: 600 weight, 56px display on desktop and 36px on mobile, tracking -0.03em. Geist Mono for timers, scores, speaker timestamps, and rubric weights. Body text is at least 16px on mobile.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 14px card radius, 10px control radius, pill chips. Hairline 1px borders plus one soft shadow on light surfaces; dark surfaces get a 1px inner top highlight. The blurred orb is retired. Persona avatars come from a seeded monogram-and-hue system, so every persona has a stable face with no image licensing.
design_language.motion: Springs for deck swipes and sheet snaps. Score rings count up over 600ms. Whisper cards slide in from the right in 200ms and dim after 8 seconds. Objection alerts pulse once. Everything collapses to fades under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke for all icons. One custom mark for the coach (a waveform inside a speech bubble) so the coach is recognizable at a glance in every mode.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default for library, progress, team, and debrief. Dark is the default for the live call and the landing hero. Both follow prefers-color-scheme with a manual toggle in the header. Every token has both values and no component hard-codes a color.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop uses a 64px icon rail that expands on hover to show labels: Practice, Library, Wizard, Progress, Team (only when an org exists), and Settings. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar: Practice, Library, Progress, More. A command palette opens from any screen for jumping to a persona, starting a drill, or opening a debrief. The live call takes over the full viewport with no rail and one End control. Existing routes (/trainer, /trainer/scenarios, /dashboard) remain valid through redirects, and /library and /wizard are added so current links keep working during migration.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The coach is a separate model stream, distinct from the persona, so the persona stays in character and never sees coaching. After every rep turn, a small GPT model reads the rolling transcript and returns structured JSON: rubric deltas, one next-best question, and an objection tag. Whisper cards appear within about two seconds of the rep's turn, cap at one visible, and dismiss on tap or after 8 seconds. Rubric meters update live with delta chips, but they are labeled 'live estimate'. The full-transcript grade still runs on the heavier model at the end, and the debrief is authoritative. Talk-track steps tick when the coach detects them. A quiet mode turns the coach off per session. Voice and text share one pipeline, and if coach latency spikes the call continues and scoring simply lags.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library ships as plain files: one persona per JSON file covering role, industry, difficulty, objections, voice, scenario, and rubric. A schema validator runs in CI so contributors can add personas by pull request. Target at launch: 150 or more built-in personas across at least 20 sales jobs (SDR cold call, AE discovery, insurance, mortgage, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections), each with an objection pack. Filters combine across job, industry, difficulty, objection type, and mode. The AI wizard accepts any source (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP, or a pasted call), drafts persona, scenario, and rubric through structured outputs, and runs a dry run before saving. Its export uses the same file format, so AI-drafted personas can go back upstream as contributions.
signature_moments: The whisper card: one amber line, about two seconds after your turn, that says exactly what to ask next.
Live rubric meters with delta chips that move while you are still talking.
Swipe to rehearse: right launches a 90-second objection drill, left skips, up saves.
An under-the-hood drawer on every debrief showing the rubric line and model behind each score.
Long-press to end the call, so nobody loses a live session to a mis-tap.
openai_fund_angle: Make OpenAI usage visible and inspectable. A model strip on the landing page and live call names the model for each role (persona voice via the OpenAI Realtime API as a first-class option alongside ElevenLabs, the coach, grading at the current gpt-4.1-mini default, and the wizard) with per-call cost. Settings gets a bring-your-own-key page. Codex is used in the repo's own workflows (PR review, persona-file validation, release notes), documented in CONTRIBUTING, which maps to the Codex for Open Source criteria: PR review, maintainer automation, and release workflows (https://developers.openai.com/community/codex-for-oss). For contributors, a Good first persona board, a wizard export that opens a pre-filled PR, and the under-the-hood drawer invite prompt and rubric improvements. The Codex open source fund application is at https://openai.com/form/codex-open-source-fund/.

inspirations.borrowed: Connecting real call insights to targeted practice, reflected in the Biggest miss card and suggested drills.
Component system on Tailwind v4 and React 19.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about one week): move tokens from tailwind.config into a Tailwind v4 CSS theme, install shadcn/ui, and map the existing .card, .btn-primary, .input, and .badge classes to shadcn variants so nothing breaks. Phase 1: app shell, landing, and dashboard. Phase 2: pre-call and live-call cockpit with the coach stream, behind a feature flag; voice path and grading API stay unchanged until this phase. Phase 3: debrief, progress, and team views. Phase 4: persona library with JSON schema and validator, then filters, deck mode, and the wizard. Playwright screenshots of all nine screens in light and dark at 390px and 1440px become the regression baseline. The shell is L; the library content and wizard push the overall effort to XL.

risks: Swipe can feel like a dating app for a serious training tool. Keep the grid as the default and the deck as an opt-in drill mode.
Coach latency: if the coach stream is slow, the call must continue and scoring must lag rather than block the rep.
Persona content is a large authoring job. A schema validator and contributor PR template are needed before claiming 150 personas.
OpenAI credit burn: a coach call every turn plus full grading can cost more per session than expected. Use the smallest adequate model, cap coach tokens, and show per-call cost.
A dark-first live call departs from the current light-only look, so both themes need testing on every screen.
Dropping three.js from the call screen and generalizing the ElevenLabs-specific UI is real migration work. Keep the voice provider behind an interface.
The heuristic fallback grading must stay visibly labeled so reviewers never mistake it for LLM grading.
